title: 1996 Granada–Dakar Rally
who: Won by Pierre Lartigue / Michel Perin (Citroën) and Edi Orioli (Yamaha)
summary: The 1996 edition of the Dakar Rally, in its African era: 17 stage towns and bivouacs through Spain, Morocco, Mauritania, Mali, Guinea, Senegal. Winners — Cars: Pierre Lartigue / Michel Perin (Citroën); Bikes: Edi Orioli (Yamaha); Trucks: Viktor Moskovskikh / Anatoliy Kouzmine (Kamaz 49252).

sources.label: Citroënët: Citroën in the Dakar in the 1990s

approximate: Stage towns and bivouacs from Wikipedia's stage table. The rally ran off-road between them, so the lines are straight from bivouac to bivouac.

stops.name: Granada
stops.text: A short prologue in Granada opens the 18th Dakar, again starting away from Paris.

stops.name: Málaga
stops.text: Stage 1 down to the coast, then the crossing to Morocco.

stops.name: Nador
stops.text: Stage 2 starts in Nador after the crossing.

stops.name: Oujda
stops.text: End of stage 2, with 149 km timed.

stops.name: Er-Rachidia
stops.text: Stage 3: 328 km timed, south to the edge of the Sahara.

stops.name: Fam El Hisn
stops.text: Stage 4: 540 km timed to Fam El Hisn.

stops.name: Smara
stops.text: Stage 5: 474 km timed into Western Sahara.

stops.name: Zouerat
stops.text: Stage 8: a 511 km loop back to Zouérat, then a rest day.

stops.name: El Mreiti
stops.text: Stage 9: 629 km timed into the empty north-east of Mauritania.

stops.name: Tichit
stops.text: Stage 10: 632 km timed to the old desert town of Tichit.

stops.name: Dakar
stops.text: The finish after a 20 km last special. Lartigue and Périn won the cars for Citroën for the third year running; Edi Orioli won the bikes on a Yamaha after Peterhansel lost time with refuelling problems.
